problem_statement: A projectile is launched from the base of an inclined plane having an angle of inclination alpha = 30.0 degrees with the horizontal. The launch speed is u = 20.0 m/s at an angle theta = 60.0 degrees with the horizontal (i.e. at 30.0 degrees above the incline). Taking downward gravity g = 10.0 m/s^2, find: (a) the time of flight T until impact on the incline, (b) the range R_up along the incline, and (c) the angle at which the projectile strikes the incline.
target_quantity: Time of flight T, range along incline R_up, impact angle with incline
governing_principles: Tilted coordinate axes: a_x' = -g sin(alpha), a_y' = -g cos(alpha)
solution_strategy: Rotate axes by alpha = 30 deg. Find T from y'(T) = 0. Evaluate x'(T) for range R_up. Evaluate velocity components v_x' and v_y' at impact to find impact direction.

ordered_steps.action_description: Resolve initial velocity and gravity into components parallel and perpendicular to the incline
ordered_steps.equation_latex: u_{x'} = u\cos(\theta - \alpha) = 20\cos 30^\circ = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}, \quad u_{y'} = u\sin(\theta - \alpha) = 20\sin 30^\circ = 10.0\text{ m/s}; \quad a_{x'} = -10\sin 30^\circ = -5.0\text{ m/s}^2, \quad a_{y'} = -10\cos 30^\circ = -5\sqrt{3}\text{ m/s}^2

ordered_steps.action_description: Determine time of flight by solving y'(T) = 0
ordered_steps.equation_latex: u_{y'} T - \frac{1}{2} g\cos\alpha T^2 = 0 \implies T = \frac{2 u_{y'}}{g\cos\alpha} = \frac{2 (10.0)}{5\sqrt{3}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{3} \approx 2.309\text{ s}
ordered_steps.justification: Condition for landing on the incline.

ordered_steps.action_description: Calculate range along incline R_up = x'(T)
ordered_steps.equation_latex: R_{\text{up}} = u_{x'} T + \frac{1}{2} a_{x'} T^2 = (10\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + \frac{1}{2}(-5.0)\left(\frac{16}{3}\right) = 40.0 - \frac{40.0}{3} = \frac{80.0}{3} \approx 26.67\text{ m}
ordered_steps.justification: Position along incline with uniform acceleration a_x' = -5 m/s^2.

ordered_steps.action_description: Evaluate parallel velocity component at impact v_x'(T)
Evaluate perpendicular velocity component at impact v_y'(T)
Compute impact angle with the incline
ordered_steps.justification: Tangent of angle between impact velocity vector and incline surface.

final_answer: (a) Time of flight T = 4/sqrt(3) s (approx 2.31 s); (b) Range up incline R_up = 80/3 m (approx 26.67 m); (c) The projectile strikes the incline at an angle of 60.0 degrees to the inclined surface.
sanity_checks: Check range formula: R_up = [2 u^2 sin(theta - alpha) cos(theta)] / [g cos^2(alpha)] = [2(400) sin(30) cos(60)] / [10 (3/4)] = [800 * (1/2) * (1/2)] / [7.5] = 200 / 7.5 = 80/3 m, exact match!
Perpendicular landing check: v_x' > 0 means the projectile does not land perpendicularly; it strikes at 60 deg.
alternate_methods: Intersect standard Cartesian parabola y = x tan(60) - gx^2/(2 u^2 cos^2 60) with line y = x tan(30).
trap_alerts: Do not forget that gravity has an acceleration component along the incline (a_x' = -g sin alpha)!
